name: Tucson International Airport
before:
Arizona's second busiest airport after Phoenix Sky Harbor, 8 miles south of downtown Tucson. It handled 1,959,789 enplanements in 2024 and flies non-stop to 23 destinations across the United States and Canada, so it is a regional airport rather than a gateway.

One layout detail to flag. Concourse C is not in the main terminal at all. It is a separate building to the west with a single gate, so a client sent to C needs directing to a different building. Concourses A and B, with nine and eleven gates, are in the main terminal.

Inside the main terminal, baggage claim and pick-up are on the ground level and ticketing, security and the gates are above.

Sun Tran bus routes 11 and 25 serve the airport. Two runways operate on a 7,938 acre site at an elevation of 2,643 feet.
after:
Arizona's second busiest airport after Phoenix Sky Harbor, 8 miles south of downtown Tucson. Preliminary FAA figures show just under 1.9 million passengers boarding flights here in 2025. The airport lists nonstop flights to 16 destinations, all in the United States, so it is a regional airport rather than a gateway.

One layout detail to flag. Concourse C is not in the main terminal at all, so a client sent to C needs directing to a different building. Concourses A and B are in the main terminal.

Inside the main terminal, baggage claim and pick-up are on the ground level and ticketing, security and the gates are above.

Sun Tran bus routes 11 and 25 serve the airport. Two runways operate at an elevation of 2,643 feet.
